successors.note: Cliopatria's Kingdom of Italy row (587..1946) opens with the Lombard kingdom; the Kingdom of Italy part of group eu-13 is to split it, so the slug may change to a Lombard-kingdom slug (kingdom-of-the-lombards). The duchy itself lasted, as a duchy inside the kingdom, until 774-797 (Tuscia page). correction.text: Lucca and the Lombard-held part of Tuscany, including Florence: the Cliopatria 577 shape held one year earlier, from the infobox date 'Established: 576'

keyframe_review.note: New one-year keyframe: Cliopatria's shape starts in 577 but the page's infobox gives 576. The text puts the first Lombard duchies 'about 574', so 576 is the page's own date for this duchy, not a measured start of the border.

17,119 km2 for 577..586. The page gives no area; it describes 'much of today's Tuscany, including Florence', the sea to the west and the Exarchate elsewhere; the province of Viterbo ('Roman Tuscia') was part of it at first and the Pisan region came under Lombard control only about half a century later, so the shape is an approximation of the border. The page says the duchy lasted to 774-797 inside the kingdom; the shape ends 586 because Cliopatria draws the restored kingdom from 587 (Kingdom of the Lombards page: dukes ruled alone from Cleph's death in 574, in 584 they agreed to crown Authari).

region.text: Lucca and the Lombard-held part of Tuscany, including Florence, with the Tyrrhenian Sea to the west and Byzantine territory (the Exarchate of Ravenna) elsewhere

ledger.note: 576: the Lombard duchy of Tuscia arises at Lucca in the ducal anarchy. Infobox 'Established: 576'; 'Lucca and Spoleto were the first Lombard duchies formed after King Alboin's death, during the period of ducal anarchy (about 574)'; 'The capital of the duchy was Lucca'.

region.text: the whole duchy, taken back under the restored Lombard crown

ledger.note: 586: the duchy's separate life ends as the Lombard kingdom is restored. The Kingdom of the Lombards page dates the restoration earlier: after Cleph's murder in 574 'another king was not appointed, and for a decade' the dukes ruled; 'in 584, the dukes agreed to crown Cleph's son, Autari'; the page gives no 586 event. The Tuscia page has Gummarito duke 576-585 and the duchy surviving to 774-797 as a Lombard duchy within the kingdom. Year 586 is Cliopatria's last shape, hence confidence 1.

certainty.note: Ducal-anarchy borders are approximate; the border with the Byzantine Exarchate was fixed only by the 680 peace (Tuscia page), long after this duchy's separate life.

notes: Cliopatria's Duchy of Tuscia is one shape (577..586). It exists as a separate polity only for the ten years of ducal rule; the Lombard duchy of Tuscia itself ran on inside the kingdom to 774-797 (page), so this dossier is the ducal-anarchy interval, and the later duchy is part of the Lombard kingdom (Cliopatria's Kingdom of Italy row 587..774), which belongs to the Kingdom of Italy part of eu-13. No infobox area on the page, so the area check against Cliopatria's 17,119 km2 is not possible. The page-budget (1-2) was met with two pages. Neither page gives a month. The Cliopatria Lombards row (577..586, 79,112 km2, lat 43.9+) is the northern kingdom during the same years and is written by group eu-06. The 576 start follows the infobox; the text says the first duchies were formed 'about 574'.
